outcome: A failed JEV judgment changes the worker's understanding before it can mutate or re-submit the candidate: the exact finding is converted into a bound lookback, diagnosis and strategy revision, making JEV a supervisory control input rather than a pass/fail gate.
currentProblem: Current Outer Blackboard publication sends a non-satisfied Worker judgment directly to WORKER/REPAIR, while delivery context treats both EXECUTION and REPAIR as action.kind=IMPLEMENT with source-write scope. This allows the actor to respond to JEV findings by immediately editing/resubmitting artifacts until the evaluator passes, without a mandatory lookback that explains what claim failed, why prior reasoning was wrong, which assumption changed, or what materially different strategy will be tried.
constraints: RESEARCH_SA only until a fresh JEV readiness judgment accepts the exact plan; this registration does not authorize implementation changes.
Preserve the two-lane Research/Worker model; do not create a third lane for supervision.
JEV remains an independent semantic judge and must not become the actor or prescribe code edits; supervisory control consumes its structured findings.
A failed judgment must not grant source-write repair authority until the actor has produced a judgment-bound lookback/reconsideration that changes epistemic state.
Agent-authored prose or artifact existence alone is not implementation evidence and must not satisfy a finding or material-delta check.
CI remains an enforcement/projection surface; local and CI paths must consume one canonical supervision/transition policy rather than separate gate semantics.
successCriteria: A non-satisfied Worker judgment cannot transition directly into an IMPLEMENT action; the next obligation is an explicit read-only lookback/reconsideration bound to the exact judgment, candidate and generation.

The lookback records failed claims, expected versus observed evidence, invalidated assumptions, causal diagnosis, strategy revision and the evidence expected from the next attempt before repair authority is granted.
Re-evaluation requires a material candidate/evidence/strategy delta that addresses prior findings; unchanged or cosmetic resubmission cannot create semantic progress.
Repeated unresolved findings trigger strategy reconsideration/escalation instead of unlimited JEV retry spam.
Local execution and CI enforcement use the same canonical supervisory transition semantics, while CI remains the final projection/gate rather than the owner of the feedback loop.
Focused negative tests prove that prose-only lookback, unchanged candidates and repeated identical repair strategies cannot advance to another accepted evaluation.
